t: You're standing at the monument to Vincent Figgins in Nunhead Cemetery, in Southwark. Figgins was a London typefounder, someone who cast and sold the metal type used in printing. After an apprenticeship with Joseph Jackson, he set up his own type foundry in 1792. The business was extremely successful, and its modern serif faces and display typefaces strongly influenced British printing styles in the nineteenth century. A successor company went on making type until the 1970s. Figgins lived from 1766 to 1844, and this monument commemorates him.
